source.title: Simplicity Bias via Global Convergence of Sharpness Minimization
source.authors: Khashayar Gatmiry; Zhi-Yuan Li; Sashank J. Reddi; S. Jegelka

record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes whether a sharpness-minimizing training procedure produces simple, low-rank features, but does not measure natural-label test error or the training–test generalization gap. Its theoretical and synthetic results bear conceptually on the simplicity-bias aspect of the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical convergence and a synthetic feature-rank experiment. The reported singular-value behavior is a feature-simplicity result, not a test-error or generalization-gap measurement. It also discusses prior-work claims, which are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves convergence and feature collapse for restricted two-layer networks and reports synthetic feature-structure experiments. None tests V1–V8. In particular, trace-Hessian minimization and feature rank do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness versus training–test gap relationship.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. More precisely, the authors prove exponential convergence of the limiting sharpness flow under their assumptions and arbitrarily accurate, high-probability guarantees for sufficiently small-step label noise SGD. Neuron pre-activations coincide on the training data; convergence of the full weight vectors to one vector additionally uses initialization in the data subspace. Lower-dimensional experiments show rank-two collapse in one setting and clustering despite high rank in another.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies label noise SGD and a Riemannian gradient flow of trace-Hessian sharpness in a two-layer network with fixed second-layer weights and synthetic data; it does not test the claim's natural-label held-out generalization setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The theoretical rank-one result depends on activation assumptions, data-matrix coherence, and a sufficiently small step size. The synthetic feature structure differs between the d > n and d < n settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Under activation, data-coherence and normality assumptions, the limiting trace-Hessian flow converges exponentially to a sharpness minimum on the zero-loss manifold. Sufficiently small-step label noise SGD reaches arbitrarily accurate approximations with high probability, with identical neuron pre-activations on the training data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the restricted two-layer model, minimizing trace-Hessian sharpness yields a rank-one training feature matrix.

fits_no_version.finding: The synthetic d = n = 3 experiment reports collapse to one surviving singular value; the d = 5, n = 6 experiment reports two surviving components.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label noise SGD can produce low-rank training features in synthetic two-layer networks.

fits_no_version.finding: In the d = 10, n = 15 experiment, the feature matrix remains high rank while neuron features cluster; the plotted subset contains 12 selected neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neuron-feature clustering can occur under label noise SGD even when the feature matrix remains high rank.

record.problems: The experiments are synthetic and report feature structure rather than held-out error. The paper states that the theory applies to a restricted two-layer setting and leaves low-dimensional inputs as a future direction. Figure-based experiments do not report numerical uncertainty.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting and held-out performance versus natural-label training.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across training-set sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps, including ranking against norm and margin measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2 classification conflicts with its own explanation that no claim version is measured. States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not dispute the reported feature-structure observations.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label memorization or natural-label held-out accuracy comparison.
No width sweep or test-error measurement.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization-gap comparison.
No removal of memorized examples or test-accuracy comparison.

rows.subject: two-layer neural network (m = 10 neurons)

rows.operation_detail: Label noise SGD with learning rate η = 0.05 and noise variance σ = 0.03 on synthetic data; tracked feature-matrix singular values over iterations.

conditions.value: synthetic; each data-point entry generated uniformly on [0, 1]

rows.measure: Feature-matrix singular values over training iterations
rows.value: The second and third eigenvalues converge to zero.
rows.note: Synthetic experiment on feature rank; it does not report held-out error or a generalization gap.
rows.check: The measured feature collapse cannot establish any claim version. Figure 1 plots singular values; replace the value's 'eigenvalues' with 'singular values'. The stated setup has d = n = 3, despite the caption describing d > n.

rows.value: Except the first and second eigenvalues of the feature matrix, the rest go to zero.
rows.note: The authors describe this as a low-dimensional setting where the feature matrix cannot be rank one; no held-out error is reported.
rows.check: Feature rank cannot establish any claim version. Section 5 reports two surviving components, but Figure 3 displays only the first three singular values; describe the result as the authors' reported rank-two collapse, and use 'singular values' rather than 'eigenvalues'.

rows.value: Most of the principal components of the neurons except possibly one outlier are converging to the same point.
